question: A jail checks `target.startsWith('/srv/workspace')`. Which request escapes it?
options: `notes/todo.md`
`/srv/workspace-backup/.env`, because the prefix matches although the folder is a sibling of the root
`./src/index.ts`
`/srv/workspace`
explanation: Compare against the root followed by a separator (`/srv/workspace/`), or accept the root itself. A bare prefix check accepts every sibling whose name starts the same way.

question: Your fetch tool blocks URLs whose text contains `127.0.0.1` or `localhost`. Why is that not enough?
options: Because those addresses are allowed by every operating system
Because the model never writes those strings
Because the same address has many spellings (`0x7f000001`, `2130706433`, `127.1`, `localhost.`); parse the URL and check the normalized hostname instead
Because URL checks should be done with regular expressions on the raw string
explanation: URL parsers normalize numeric and dotted forms to one canonical address. Check what the parser produced, which is also what the HTTP client will connect to.

question: `https://docs.example.com/page` is allowlisted and answers `302 Location: http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/`. What should the fetch tool do?
options: Follow it: the original URL was allowed
Fetch with manual redirects, check the redirect target against the same policy, and refuse it
Follow it but hide the response from the model
Retry the original URL until it stops redirecting
explanation: Each redirect is a new request. An open redirect on an allowed host is a classic way to reach cloud metadata or internal services.

question: The agent has a shell tool, and your `read_file` tool enforces a perfect path jail. Is the workspace protected?
options: Yes: the jail covers every file access
Yes, as long as the permission policy denies `cat`
No: a shell command can open any file the process can reach; the boundary must be an OS sandbox or a container
No, because path jails never work on Linux
explanation: Tool-level checks only cover the tools you wrote. Once arbitrary processes run, isolation has to come from below: OS sandboxing, containers or microVMs.

question: Why does the dispatcher return `Error: path_escape: ...` as a tool message instead of throwing?
options: So the loop keeps running, the model learns the boundary and can try a legitimate call, and the harness logs the attempt
Because tool messages are cheaper than exceptions
Because the model can override the error if it insists
Because thrown errors are invisible to the harness
explanation: A crash ends the task; a clear refusal lets the agent recover. Repeated escape attempts are also a useful signal of prompt injection.
